title: Conformalized Link Prediction on Graph Neural Networks

problem.claim: Unreliable GNN predictions hinder applications in high-stakes domains.

gap.claim: Existing uncertainty quantification methods often lack rigorous uncertainty estimates.

contributions.claim: A distribution-free and model-agnostic uncertainty quantification approach constructs predictive intervals for GNN-based link prediction with a statistical guarantee.
The work establishes a permutation invariance condition for applying conformal prediction to link prediction tasks, together with exact test-time coverage.
A sampling-based method aligns graph structure with a power-law distribution before standard conformal prediction.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe this work as the first attempt to introduce the proposed uncertainty quantification approach for GNN-based link prediction.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The approach achieves the desired marginal coverage in extensive experiments.
The approach significantly improves conformal prediction efficiency compared with baseline methods.
The work theoretically and empirically establishes the stated permutation invariance condition.

narrative_sequence.summary: GNN predictions can be unreliable in high-stakes applications, while existing uncertainty estimates are often insufficiently rigorous.
The work applies conformal prediction to construct statistically guaranteed intervals for GNN link prediction and identifies graph dependence and efficiency as central challenges.
It establishes a permutation invariance condition, connects power-law adherence with conformal prediction efficiency, and introduces a sampling-based structural alignment method.
Extensive experiments report desired marginal coverage and improved efficiency over baselines.

source_observation.claim: For dependent graph data, the validity of conformal prediction depends on establishing an appropriate invariance condition.

interpretation.claim: Uncertainty methods for structured data should explicitly address whether their statistical assumptions survive dependence.

application.claim: When adapting a statistical calibration method to graphs, test or prove a graph-specific invariance condition before relying on its guarantees.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the condition's formal scope, required graph settings, or limitations.

source_observation.claim: The approach uses graph structural information and power-law alignment to improve conformal prediction efficiency.

interpretation.claim: Exploiting domain structure can improve the usefulness of statistically valid prediction sets or intervals.

application.claim: For structured prediction, consider preprocessing or sampling strategies that align data with empirically or theoretically relevant structural priors.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the efficiency benefit extends to graphs that do not adhere to a power-law distribution.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the exact predictive interval construction or sampling algorithm.
The abstract does not report datasets, baseline identities, numerical coverage, efficiency, or interval-length results.
The abstract does not describe the formal permutation invariance condition or its assumptions.
The abstract does not provide independent verification or reproducibility details.
